title: Ashvamedhika
hook: Abhimanyu's son is born without breath, and the women of the house turn to Krishna
carry: a kept promise, a true sentence

segments.voice: Yesterday in Ashvamedhika, Uttanka refused water from an outcast hunter who turned out to be Indra, carrying amrita. Your line was because of who was holding the cup. Did help come from somewhere unexpected? Day eight hundred seventy.

There's a weapon we've already met in this serial. After the night raid, Ashvatthama loosed a terrible weapon he couldn't call back, and he turned it on the wombs of the Pandava women. Krishna answered him then with a promise: the child Uttara is carrying will live. Now the Pandavas are away in the mountains, fetching Marutta's gold. Uttara, Abhimanyu's young widow, goes into labor. The child is born, and he doesn't breathe. Kunti, Draupadi, Subhadra and Uttara herself are in that room. Today, the promise is called in.
screen: `ASHVATTHAMA'S WEAPON.` → `KRISHNA'S PROMISE.` → `A CHILD BORN WITHOUT BREATH.`

segments.voice: The grief in the epic here is not quiet. Kunti, the grandmother of Abhimanyu, reminds Krishna of what he said: you promised this child would live. Subhadra, Krishna's own sister and Abhimanyu's mother, pleads with him. And Uttara speaks to the still baby in her arms, in Ganguli's telling, as if he could hear her: your father died young, and now you have gone after him. Krishna goes into the birth room. Then he does something the epic takes care to describe. He doesn't bargain or chant a spell. He makes a declaration of truth. In this tradition, a true statement, solemnly spoken, has power. Krishna names truths about his own life: that he has not spoken a falsehood, not even in jest, that he has not turned his back in battle, that righteousness is dear to him. And by the force of those truths, he says, let this child live. The child stirs, and breathes. The house that was wailing is filled with joy. This boy is Parikshit, and the dynasty that was nearly erased will go on through him. Later he'll be king. Notice where the life comes from in this scene. Not from a weapon, and not from a trick. From a life lived truthfully, spoken out loud at the moment it's needed. During the war, a half-truth from Yudhishthira brought Drona down. Here, at the cradle, a kept promise and a true sentence bring a child back.
screen: `KUNTI: "YOU PROMISED"` · `UTTARA SPEAKS TO HER SON` · `A DECLARATION OF TRUTH` · then, large: `PARIKSHIT BREATHES`

segments.voice: Sit, and let both feet rest on the ground. Bring to mind one promise you've made that you're still keeping, small or large, to a child, a friend, a parent, yourself. Breathe in and name it plainly. Breathe out and notice its weight, without hurry. Then name one true thing about how you try to live, one sentence you could say out loud and mean. If you pray, you can offer that sentence in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Ashvamedhika. The book where a child born without breath lives, by a promise kept and a truth spoken aloud.
Your line: a kept promise, a true sentence. Today, keep one small promise exactly as you said it, even if no one would notice. Day eight hundred seventy.

howItsDone: Parikshit's revival is told in the Ashvamedhika Parva, and Hindu tradition remembers Parikshit as the king to whom, in the Bhagavata Purana, the sage Shuka later recites that text.

fork.setup: you're Krishna. the child you promised would live is born without breath, and his family turns to you. what do you do?
options: call down a weapon against Ashvatthama.
declare the truths of your own life.
tell them nothing can be done.
fork.reveal: Krishna makes a solemn declaration of truth, and by its force the child breathes.

original.note: Parikshit: Abhimanyu's son, revived at birth, later king.

trapdoor: what you thought: Krishna revives the child with divine power alone.
what it means: he does it by declaring the truths of his own life.
what a scholar hears: this is an act of truth, where a solemnly spoken true statement is given the force to bring back a life.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm the list of truths Krishna declares (never a falsehood even in jest, never turning back in battle, love of righteousness) against Ganguli.
Confirm that the Pandavas are away fetching Marutta's treasure at the time of the birth, and which women are present.
